name: Starting battery open-circuit voltage
location: Directly across the positive and negative posts of the machine's nominal 12 V starting battery; use the lead posts, not a convenient chassis ground.
procedure_ref: Connect a calibrated DVOM red lead to battery positive and black lead to battery negative with loads off. Allow any surface charge to be removed by the battery service procedure before judging condition. Nominal system identity: TUG Model 660-28 Operation Manual CD397-Oper, Table Operation-3-4, PDF page 95. Resting-voltage acceptance range and battery condition criteria: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Starting battery voltage while cranking
location: Across the same starting-battery posts while an assistant commands START with the required operator and safety interlocks satisfied.
procedure_ref: Keep the DVOM on the battery posts, stand leads clear of belts and fans, and record the minimum stable voltage during a normal start command. Do not extend cranking or bypass an interlock for a reading. Minimum cranking voltage and maximum cranking duration: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Starter positive-feed voltage drop under load
location: From the battery positive lead post to the starter main B+ stud; if access is unsafe, divide the feed into accessible segments using the wiring diagram rather than reaching into a moving assembly.
procedure_ref: Connect the DVOM red lead to the battery positive post and black lead to the starter B+ stud, then measure only while cranking. The reading represents drop across the complete positive feed. Inspect each cable, lug, connection, and series contact by segment if excessive. Maximum allowable drop: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Starter ground-side voltage drop under load
location: From the starter motor housing or manufacturer-designated starter ground point to the battery negative lead post.
procedure_ref: Connect the DVOM red lead to the clean starter ground point and black lead directly to battery negative, then measure while cranking. The reading exposes unwanted engine/chassis/battery-return resistance. Do not assume a shiny chassis connection proves a good return. Maximum allowable drop: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Starter solenoid control (S) terminal voltage
location: At the starter solenoid S/control terminal identified in the applicable 660-28 wiring diagram, measured to battery negative while START is commanded.
procedure_ref: Back-probe with a suitable insulated adapter; do not pierce insulation or short adjacent B+ terminals. Record control voltage during a normal START command and note whether the solenoid clicks. Acceptance against battery voltage and allowable control-circuit drop: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Neutral-start interlock output voltage
location: At the output side of the neutral-start switch shown in the serial-specific 660-28 wiring diagram, measured to battery negative with START commanded and the transmission selector confirmed in neutral.
procedure_ref: Identify the correct switch and wire from the schematic before back-probing. Check actual connector position and mechanical selector alignment rather than relying only on the shift lever position. Do not jumper the interlock. Output-voltage acceptance: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Charging voltage at starting battery
location: Across the starting-battery posts with the engine running at the manual-specified speed and electrical-load condition.
procedure_ref: Use a calibrated DVOM directly on the battery posts. Record idle and loaded readings only at conditions given in the charging-system procedure; keep leads away from belts and fans and never remove a battery cable as a charging test. Alternator rating is listed as 95 A in TUG Model 660-28 Operation Manual CD397-Oper, Table Operation-3-4, PDF page 95, but that rating is not a voltage acceptance range. Charging voltage range and test conditions: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Main hydraulic relief pressure setting
location: At the main-system pressure test point identified by the serial-specific hydraulic schematic. The listed main setting must not be applied to the steering or front-cylinder-down circuits.
spec_source: TUG Model 660-28 Operation Manual CD397-Oper, Operation-3-9, Table Operation-3-13, PDF page 101 (August 2018 Rev B page)
procedure_ref: The cited table lists a 1,500 psi main relief setting and 1,500 psi maximum system pressure; it gives no gauge tolerance. Before connecting a gauge, verify the exact port, rated fittings, oil-temperature condition, engine speed, lift command, and relief-check procedure in the serial-specific maintenance manual. A single-value spec_min/spec_max is the published setting, not permission to hold a function at relief indefinitely. Gauge tolerance and detailed measurement acceptance: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Steering hydraulic relief pressure setting
location: At the steering-system pressure test point identified by the serial-specific hydraulic schematic, not the main-lift circuit port.
spec_source: TUG Model 660-28 Operation Manual CD397-Oper, Operation-3-9, Table Operation-3-13, PDF page 101 (August 2018 Rev B page)
procedure_ref: The cited table lists a 1,000 psi steering relief setting and gives no gauge tolerance. Verify steering test-port identity, rated gauge/fittings, oil temperature, engine speed, steering command, and tire-clearance procedure before testing. Chock the machine and keep the steering path clear. Gauge tolerance and detailed measurement acceptance: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Power Stow auxiliary battery voltage, each battery
location: Across the posts of each individual 12 V Power Stow battery, one battery at a time; identify series links and isolation devices before disconnecting anything.
procedure_ref: Power Stow 600i Maintenance Manual Rev E (Delta), PDF page 4, includes testing the 12 V batteries and replacing them in pairs. Use a calibrated DVOM on each battery's own posts, then repeat with the prescribed hydraulic load if the manual permits. Resting/load-voltage range, pair-matching criterion, and load-test acceptance: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Power Stow main lift-pump outlet pressure
location: At the main lift-pressure test port identified on the correct Power Stow serial-specific hydraulic schematic. Exact port ID and physical location must be verified; do not tee into an unidentified hose or adapt a base-chassis port without a matching procedure.
procedure_ref: Install a calibrated pressure gauge and rated fittings only after isolation and manufacturer-approved pressure release. Re-energize solely for the documented lift-pressure test and record oil temperature, pump drive condition, control command, and stabilized reading. Do not deadhead or hold at relief unless the manual directs it. Port ID, target range, tolerance, and detailed test conditions: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Loading-head lift cylinder cap-end pressure
location: At the manufacturer-provided cap-end cylinder test point, if fitted, or the approved diagnostic connection shown on the Power Stow schematic. Do not loosen a cylinder hose merely to create a test point.
procedure_ref: Support and unload the loading head as directed before access. Install the gauge with stored pressure isolated, then use only the documented cap-end pressure command to determine whether pump pressure actually reaches the cylinder. Port, support, test command, and pressure range: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Loading-head lift cylinder rod-end/back-pressure
location: At the manufacturer-provided rod-end/return test point, if fitted, or the approved diagnostic connection shown on the Power Stow schematic. Exact port ID must be verified before connection.
procedure_ref: Use the manufacturer-supported and unloaded configuration. Measure rod-end pressure/back-pressure only in the prescribed lift or hold test to distinguish return/check/counterbalance restriction from internal cylinder leakage. Port, command, hold time, and acceptance range: TODO: needs spec from manual.

name: Power Stow lift-pump delivery flow
location: Through the manufacturer-approved inline flow-test connection between the lift pump outlet and control circuit; only a flow meter, load valve, hoses, and fittings rated for the circuit may be used.
procedure_ref: A qualified technician must install the bidirectional-correct flow/pressure test set after isolation, then apply only the manual-specified loading and pump-drive conditions. Never close a load valve as a substitute for knowing the relief setting and test limit. Flow range, pressure/load condition, and operating temperature: TODO: needs spec from manual.
